title: Home is a nest, not a point: gravity, dug chambers, queen, brood (side view)
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Real ants home to the entrance by a drifting vector, and inside by gravity, memory and chamber road signs; nests are shafts and chambers with jobs (royal, brood, store, reception, midden); the queen's scent marks her, not home; losing the only queen orphans a colony. Today: one pre-dug chamber, an exact vector to it through soil, a single home field, food and births as scalars.

title: Unity needs contact: underground, the colonies never meet, and 'unified' is reached without a meeting
description:
PRD §22. On the underground default world (#8), seeds 1–3 at 300 + 300 ants, the two colonies never meet in 10 sim-minutes (0 deaths even with no fungus). Garden painted on both nests still reaches "unified" at ~105 s: the nests' odours converge and the "quiet minute" is quiet only because nobody was ever in contact.

Fix: unified should also require that the colonies have met as allies, e.g. a fading count of allied contacts (the fungus already classifies a host's contact as kin / allied / strangers; Game can count ants of either colony with an allied neighbour) above a floor in the last minute, and the unity meter should show it. Then re-measure open and underground. Separately, underground games may need the colonies' tunnels to meet before unity is possible at all — a world question for the underground MR's follow-ups.

title: Fungus 1e: the fungus policy + interventions (per colony first)
description:
docs/fungus-policy.md §5, §8 (piece 5). Depends on 1a–1d.

The fungus policy picks ONE intervention per host — a preset bundle of the levers from 1b/1c/1d. Interventions: dormant, sporulate, soothe, blend, share, roam, and cull (lethal; strain-gated, so a non-lethal strain omits it).

- Start with a free LOCAL fungus rule (the baseline Jev is measured against), per colony first (one intervention per colony every ~10 s from a coarse view) before the per-host lane. Example rule: groomed → dormant; strangers near → soothe; calm contact while apart → blend; foraging on border → share; low load at home → sporulate.
- The fungus's own situation (§5.2): load, hostActivity, ground, contact, groomed, apart = 648 possible; a run meets far fewer.
- The player's levers on the policy (§5.1): strain (which interventions/caps exist), aim (goal in words), menu (options on/off), thresholds (tune the local rule). Wire at least the strain gate (cull) and the menu here.
- Jev for the fungus lane: cached per fungal situation under the player's aim, in its own lane (never in an ant request). Can follow once the local rule plays well — file as a follow-up if not done here.

Tests: the ant request for an infected host is byte-identical to a healthy ant's in the same perceived situation (the policy never enters an ant request); a cull-less strain never yields a lethal intervention.

Cost: report tokens/question for the fungus lane (npm run colony-cost + stand-in) in the PR.
close_reason: Done: fungal situation per host (648/strain), Fungus.choose gate (strain allows ∩ menu, lethal needs both), cull (odour weapon, Bloom only, off by default), dormant shows a quarter (hide works), player levers (menu, hide/cull settings, aim), local rule = strain defaults + settings (4 situational rules measured, none beat it), Jev fungus lane (fungusBrain.ts + third lane in colonyJev, cached per aim+menu, never in ant requests), ~323 tok/fungal situation, ~$0.002–0.004 per aim. 17 tests; suite timeout 60 s (file-level). PRD §18.

title: Fungus 1c: recognition — pacify, blending odour, unity meter
description:
docs/fungus-policy.md §4.B, §1, §8 (piece 3). Depends on 1a.

- B1 pacifying odour (emission): other ants weight an infected ant × (1 − p·load) when counting enemies — in resolveFights (battle.ts) and in the enemy: near check (#enemyHeading).
- B3 blending odour: each ant carries an `odour` scalar (player 0, rival 1). At its nest it relaxes toward the nest's odour; the nest drifts toward its ants; an infected host also relaxes toward ants it touches, at a rate ∝ load. Enemy only when |odour_i − odour_j| > τ. Enemy grids binned by odour (e.g. 8 bins, one CountGrid each).
- B4 tolerance: τ per ant; damp the attack-turn (turnRate×2).
- Unity meter (§1): peace (deaths/min), recognition (nest-odour distance), mixing. Panel shows it; a "unified" outcome (nest odours within τ and no fight deaths for 60 sim-s) beside won/lost.

Tests: two colonies sharing contacts converge monotonically (one-way relaxation, clamped rates — no overshoot); fights stop once inside τ.
close_reason: Done: odour per ant (nest gestalt + fungal share), strangers by odour band (recognition.ts) for fights, perception and the strategist; calm (B1), tolerance (B4), fungal odour share (B3/B7, Garden strain); unity meter + unified outcome; kin are not raided; ants coloured by odour. No fungus = identical fights (tested ant for ant). Garden both nests unifies at 150–185 s, deaths ÷20–30. 12 tests; PRD §17.

title: Fungus 1b: perception layer (the host's bent perceived state)
description:
docs/fungus-policy.md §2, §4.A, §8 (piece 2). Depends on 1a.

One distortion step between #sense (colony.ts:323) and BOTH the situation (colony.ts:415) AND steering — they must read the same bent sensors, or the host decides by one world and walks in another (§6 failure mode 5).

Levers, each scaled by load:
- A1 food-scent gain ×0–3
- A2 home-scent gain ×0–3
- A3 rival-trail reading: #sense adds w × foreign.fields.food; Game sets c.foreign = other.ph the way it sets c.enemies
- A4 alarm gain ×0–3
- A10 the host's clock: patience × factor (moves when `tired` turns on)

The host's own policy (local rule or Jev + colony doctrine) is called UNCHANGED — same Situation type, same encode, same cache key.

Tests: food gain 0 makes a follower lose a trail; foreign weight > 0 lets an infected host reach the rival's food along the rival's trail; the ant request/Situation built for an infected host is byte-identical to a healthy ant's in the same perceived state.
close_reason: Done: per-ant perception arrays (food/home/alarm gains, rival food trail, clock) applied in #sense so steering and situation agree; interventions dormant/soothe/share/roam lerped by load; strain default expression until ja-t4d.5; follow card shows bent senses. Request/situation/cache key unchanged (byte-identical request test). 7 tests; PRD §16.

title: Fungus 1a: infection state, contact spread, grooming, spore brush
description:
docs/fungus-policy.md §4.S, §5.1, §8 (piece 1). The foundation; blocks 1b/1c/1d.

- Two typed arrays on the ant structure of arrays (web/src/colony/colony.ts): `load` (Float32, 0..1) and `expr` (Uint8, the intervention running in that host; just carried for now).
- S1 Transmission: each tick a host gains β × Σ load of ants in its 3×3 cells, across BOTH colonies — reuse the neighbourhood battle.ts already scans with block sums (CountGrid). Lives in game.ts (it sees both colonies), like resolveFights.
- Grooming + decay: a visible host next to healthy nestmates loses load (and the groomer gains a small dose → later resistance); load decays slowly, or not at all for a persistent strain.
- S2 Visibility: how much load shows (a strain param), the hook grooming/rejection read.
- W3 Spore brush: a third brush beside lure/alarm (useColony.ts:29, BRUSHES) that raises load on ground + ants in the stroke with the loaded strain. It does NOT pick interventions.

Tests (node --test): a loaded ant among clean ants raises their load; an isolated ant is unchanged; grooming lowers visible load; transmission is symmetric across colonies.
close_reason: Done: load/strain/resist/expr per ant; contact transmission across colonies (frequency-dependent), grooming of visible load, priming; spore brush with Lockpick and Bloom strains; order-independent; 0.1 s step + one-chunk fast path (+0.65 ms worst case at 512x320). 14 tests; PRD §15.

title: MR: fungus 1 — the player is the fungus (perceived-state mechanics)
description:
First slice of the fungus game (docs/fungus-policy.md §8). The player is the fungus and nothing else: it never decides for an ant. Each colony keeps its own policy, doctrine, 1,296 situations and cache unchanged. The fungus bends a host's PERCEIVED state and acts through emission, body and spread levers; the host's own policy then chooses from that bent state. Win via a unity meter (§1), not won/lost.

Five child issues (ja prefix), pure TypeScript in web/src/colony/, node --test. Build order: 1a blocks 1b/1c/1d; 1e depends on 1a–1d. One PR for the milestone, agent review before merge.

Decisions (docs §9): player is only the fungus; other organisms later (a strain is a trait set); the fungus may kill but only strain-gated (cull); the policy picks interventions while the player shapes the policy via the five levers in §5.1 (brush, strain, aim, menu, thresholds).

Cost (CLAUDE.md): note tokens/ant with infection on (bent perception may reach rarely-met situations), and tokens/question for any new Jev fungus lane, in the PR. Measure with npm run colony-cost + a fungus stand-in.
close_reason: Merged: PR #7 (fungus 1a–1e, local sensing, no colony is the player's; PRD §15–23). Follow-ups filed as their own beads (ja-9xx, ja-i0f, ja-192, ja-ytc, ja-1u2, ja-d87, ja-260, ja-5tg).

title: Cached 'return' can park ants at the nest (situation can't tell an ant is already home)
description: Review of #3 (plausible, depends on live Jev). An ant that just put food down is asked as return|fresh|...|home strong; a cached 'return' keeps it at the nest forever (never tired: since resets there). Simulated: food stored stalls at ~half. Fix candidates: a mechanic that sends an ant arriving home in return mode back out (mark the situation asked so it isn't re-asked until it changes), or an atNest field. Fold into MR 7.
notes: Review of nest slice 3: the place field only moved the question (and not on top-down maps). Fixed in both views by a mechanic: an ant resting at home in return for REST (10 s) is asked afresh as an explorer; test with a stubborn policy (300/300 parked without it).
close_reason: Answered by nest slice 3 (PRD §32): an ant home in the royal chamber is asked 'royal', not 'home trail strong' (side view)

title: Pellet carriers climbing out of wide chambers by straight line + Bug2 can wander for minutes
description: Nest slice 2 (PRD §31): seed 6 colony 0 reached 5.6% out >120 s, most of them pellet carriers underground in wide chambers near the top. They head for the exact hole (no vector: they climb) and steer straight with Bug2 in open chambers. Ideas: climb by gravity at chamber exits (the highest exit), road signs toward the shaft (slice 3 marks), or the tunnel walker's stall rule in chambers.

title: Nest 8: the fungus on the new home: chamber-mark levers, nest ground, queen and brood infection
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Hosts misread chamber marks (perception gains per role); fungal ground becomes own chamber role / own tunnel / surface / foreign; queen and brood infection lethal or sterilising, strain-gated, off by default (a queen infection orphans the colony); the midden as hygiene or spore site; nest odour drifts toward the royal chamber. Bump FUNGUS_BRAIN_VERSION. Measure: unity and deaths against PRD §22.

title: Nest 4: queen and brood; births from pupae; queen loss orphans the colony
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Queen in the royal chamber lays at a rate fed by food brought to her; egg → larva (fed) → pupa → worker, replacing larder → spawn (colony.ts:1589). Queen pheromone draws nurses; nurses carry brood to her and by depth. Queen death: orphaned (no new workers; brood in progress finishes; workers age out); fallen stays 'no workers'. The in-colony part of ja-1vg.

title: Nest 3: chamber roles and floor marks (road signs); the situation's in-nest field
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Roles royal/brood/store/reception/midden; workers lay their chamber's mark, junctions keep what lies down each branch (Heyman et al. 2017). Inside the nest the mark of where an ant is going replaces homeTrail. Answers ja-qnx (an ant knows it is home). Measure: tokens per ant situation (today ~235) and situations per game; note both in the PR.

title: Nest 2: ants dig chambers off shafts, regulated by crowding and drawn to brood
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Chambers ~1 row high, widened off shafts. Dig while floor per worker < target (Odontomachus ~2 cm² per worker; folds in ja-wii), more where brood lies (leaf-cutters). Measure: floor per worker; depth profile top-heavy with gaps growing with depth (Tschinkel). Backfill must not fill a chamber with a role.
close_reason: Built (PRD §31): chambers dug off tunnels, regulated by floor per ant underground; depth profile gaps grow with depth; dug -34%

title: Nest 1: gravity sense and a noisy home vector; no vector to the chamber underground
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Down is a sense. On the surface the vector to the entrance drifts ~10% of distance and resets in the shaft (Wehner); entrance odour and the hole pull ants in. Underground: gravity + last-junction memory + road signs (slice 3), no toNest (colony.ts:1227). Measure: homing success and stuck share against ja-cwu / ja-ipu.

title: Hex underground: carriers out long round hollowed-out nests (20–27% out >120 s vs MR7 8–23%)
description: After MR8 (hex grid + meander) the economy underground is unchanged (~680 food/colony at 600 s) but more ants stay out long, and some seeds start slowly (player's first food 3–4 min on seeds 1, 2). Cause seen in traces: digging hollows the ground round each nest into a cavern with soil specks; carriers follow walls round the specks (Bug2 by cell); home-scent branch choice applies only in strict tunnel cells. Tried without clear gain: scent walking in any dug cell beside soil (seed 1 better, seed 2 worse); fewer tunnel starts (digging unchanged ~3000 cells). Ideas: density-regulated digging near the nest (ja-wii), home-vector leave from walls in open dug ground, scent climbing over a hex disc in caverns. See PRD §15.
notes: Nest slice 0 (PRD §29) ported TUNNEL_STALL to hexes: side view out>120 s seed 1 17%->0.4%, seed 2 0.1%, seed 3 18%->11% (worst sample 56%).
close_reason: MR9: wall-following fixes (no sharp hand-turn spin, line home re-anchored per soil wall, leave where the way home is open): out >120 s 2-7% mean (MR8 20-27%, MR7 8-23%), stall scan 0 (MR8 151). PRD §16.

title: Measure the fungus lane live: tokens per fungal situation, and does Jev under an aim beat the strains' defaults?
Underground homing: cut the remaining stuck share (~15 % of trips out >120 s, seeds 1–3)
description: After MR7 homing in tunnels picks the branch with the most home scent and wall-follows chambers cell by cell; ants out >120 s underground are still 6-18% mean over seeds 1-3 (open ground 1%). Remaining cases: carriers following chamber walls through big dug-out areas round the nests, and junctions where home scent is flat. Ideas: home-vector tie-break at branches; leave a chamber wall when the home vector points into open ground; see scratchpad stuck.mts in the MR7 session. Current figure (PRD §14, after the review fixes): ~15 % of trips out >120 s underground, mean over seeds 1–3; the earlier 6–25 % / 8–23 % figures predate those fixes.

title: Density-regulated digging: excavation volume still grows (social digChance added in MR9)

title: Fungus budget: spores and interventions cost biomass, so the brush is a choice
description:
Measured in ja-t4d.3 (PRD §17): painting Garden on both nests unifies the colonies in 150–185 s on every seed, and nothing costs the fungus anything. The design's strain lever (docs/fungus-policy.md §5.1, lever 2) has a cost budget: the stealth-against-potency dial set per strain.

- The fungus has biomass: it grows with load carried (hosts feed it) and with spores taken up, and the brush spends it per cell painted.
- Stronger levers (calm, mask, perception gains) cost upkeep per host; a dormant host is cheap.
- The panel shows biomass, and the brush greys out when it is spent.
- Re-measure time-to-unified with a starting budget; the goal is a game, not a 3-minute paint job.

title: Senses-only homing: ~3 % of a colony can still stall on hard maps
description: After replacing the walking-distance map with path integration + Bug2 wall-following (ed1fcef): seeds 1-10, 600 s, UI defaults: <= 7 % of a colony out > 120 s (16 of 20 runs <= 5 %), truly stalled (no progress in the next 30 s) <= ~3 % (seed 2: 15/570, seed 10: 17/593, seed 7 rival: 16/900). Most stalled ants are in give-up wander after 120 s of wall-following (long perimeters, the map edge). Ideas within the senses-only rule: climb a strong home trail while wall-following (outbound ants' trails encode routes round obstacles), remember the last exit point, smarter side choice.

title: Reframe the colony page for the player-as-fungus: no 'your' colony
description:
Decision (docs/fungus-policy.md §9): the player is only the fungus. The page and game still frame the player as colony 0: "you" vs "rival" in the stats and infection tables, the won/lost banner ("Your colony is gone"), the header comment, AntCard sides, and Jev steers only colony 0 (the rival always runs the local rule).

- Neutral colony names (e.g. by nest or colour) in the panel, follow card and banner.
- Both colonies on equal footing: each its own doctrine and its own policy (local rule or Jev); Jev for the second colony is a cost note (one more doctrine's cache).
- The outcome: unity (ja-t4d.3's unity meter / "unified") instead of won/lost; a colony beaten is a loss for the fungus (it lost hosts), not a win.
- Game.player / Game.rival naming in game.ts and useColony.ts.

Found while building ja-t4d.1. Best landed with or after ja-t4d.3 (unity outcome).
close_reason: Done: colonies named Ink/Amber by colour; outcome unified (fungus win) / fallen (a colony gone: fungus loss); both colonies on Jev under their own doctrines (ColonyJev.attachColonies, caches and in-flight by context across colonies); doctrines moved to a Colonies section as each colony's nature; summary sums every colony; fixed explain's in-flight check. 3 new tests; stack outcome test updated. PRD §20.

title: Fungus 1d: emission levers (deposit gain, cross-laying, silent fights)
description:
docs/fungus-policy.md §4.C, §8 (piece 4). Depends on 1a.

- C1 deposit gain ×0–3 (p.deposit, colony.ts:462).
- C2 cross-laying: an infected carrier's food deposit also lands in the rival's food field (a second deposit on c.foreign).
- C3 silent fights: a host in a fight lays less alarm (FightParams.alarm × (1 − load), resolveFights).

Tests: silent hosts in a fixed-seed skirmish recruit fewer defenders (less alarm laid); a cross-laying carrier raises the rival's food field along its path.
close_reason: Done: layGain (C1), crossLay into the rival's food field (C2), quiet fights (C3) as per-ant arrays written from the intervention; soothe +quiet, share +lay/crossLay; exact as-is (bench unchanged). 5 tests. Game effect mixed (seed 1 Lockpick losses halved, others ~same): tools for the policy. PRD §18.

title: MR 10: lifetime layer
description: IndexedDB autosave and slots; no won/lost; queens, nuptial flights, daughter colonies, lineage; seed rain, corpses as food, aphids; day/night and seasons; chronicle; lifetime Jev ledger and cap.

title: MR 9: endless world
description: Generate chunks on demand near any ant/nest/camera; sleeping chunks keep only deltas; wild colonies in fresh chunks; minimap fog of war; memory budget test.

title: MR 8: species framework, wave 1, several rivals
description: colony/species.ts; N colonies in game.ts with alliance ids; player picks a species. Wave 1: garden ant, fire ant, Pharaoh ant (budding), desert ant (no trails, site fidelity). Species trait line in Jev state and cache context; note tokens/ant.
notes: Fungus (2026-11-01, docs/fungus-policy.md §10): with N colonies, odour becomes a point on a disc (colonies on the rim, the fungus's odour at the centre; recognition bands become a 2D lattice); unity becomes a graph (colonies allied when nests are within tolerance; connected allies = a supercolony = MR 8's alliance id; unified = one group + a quiet minute); Colony.foreign and raidTarget become plural (raids target the nearest stranger nest). Species: strains get a host range (host-specific fungi: Pandora formicae, Ophiocordyceps); species carry an odour dimension the fungal share cannot erase, so between species the goal is parabiosis (tolerance + shared trails, each keeps its odour), within a species a merge. The fungus policy itself is already colony-count agnostic (local 'allied' contact, PRD §19).

title: Nest 9: design for MR 8: several queens, adoption, orphans merging (a unification route)
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Polygyny and queen adoption per species (ja-8fd). Speculative unification path: an orphaned colony merging into a neighbour it tolerates (same odour via Garden). Design note only.

title: Nest 6: age and zoning: young nurse deep, old forage
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Per-ant age; young near queen and brood, middle dig and carry, oldest forage (Tschinkel). Age as a perception/assignment input; prerequisite for castes (ja-jhd). Measure: where ants are by age.

title: Nest 7: the midden: refuse and corpses carried out, a boundary
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Corpses (later spent garden) carried to a midden at the mound's edge (harvesters) or a deep chamber (Atta cephalotes). Middens deter other ants (P. badius). Measure: corpses cleared; effect on raids.

title: Nest 5: food flow: reception at the top, stores deep, fed to brood and queen
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Foragers drop in reception (harvester ants: top chambers), inside workers carry down to store (granaries 20–80 cm, Tschinkel & Kwapich), then to brood and queen. stored/larder become food lying in chambers. Measure: food home; carries per food.

title: Cull's odour push depends on which side of 0.5 the nest's odour has drifted to
description: PR #7 review, unconfirmed. Recognition.step pushes a culled host's odour by 0.5 away from its nest's odour, toward the far side; zero if the nest is exactly 0.5. After Garden drifts the nests (e.g. 0.3 / 0.7), a culled host lands within tolerance of the other nest, so 'both colonies take it for a stranger' no longer holds. Push to the band farthest from every nest, or define the weapon by distance from every colony.

title: ColonyJev: 429 re-queue lost after a doctrine switch leaves ants on the local rule
description: PR #7 review, unconfirmed. On 429 the re-queue is dropped when the lane's context changed or the lane is orphaned; another colony's lane on the old context had already removed the item and nothing calls reconsider, so those ants stay local until some other reply lands. Self-heals on any later reply.

title: Fungus lane may starve: #cycle fills the in-flight slots in fixed order, fungus last
description: PR #7 review, unconfirmed. ColonyJev.#cycle fills the 2 in-flight slots lane by lane (colony 0 stances, modes, colony 1 ..., fungus last). While mode queues refill early in a game, the fungus lane (and colony 1 under its own doctrine) may wait several cycles. Measure queue age per lane; round-robin if it matters.

title: Hex grid tick cost: +23% underground / +33% open vs MR7
description: MR8 bench (1200+1200 ants): underground 3.7 vs 3.0 ms, open 5.2 vs 3.9 ms. Spread over the 6-neighbour scent stencil (#edgeCell via #at per neighbour), hex disc windows in #enemyHeading / resolveFights, tunnel checks. Ideas: specialised border loops for the 6 stencil, cache ant cells for fights in Game, precomputed neighbour index tables per parity.

title: Endless map: generate soil, chambers and food per chunk as the colony digs outward
description: World generation is position-pure per chunk (heightAt / chamberAt), but nest/food placement and the reachability prune are whole-map. For the endless map (lifetime game), generate a chunk's soil and food when a tunnel reaches its edge, with placement rules that only look at that chunk and its neighbours; reachability by digging is automatic underground (no rock seals: check per chunk).

title: Pellet scent and Atta-like backfill (MR11 backfills unused dead ends: 0.6% of dug soil)
description: MR11: pellet carriers >3 s into a trip fill a neighbouring unused dead end (no food, no food/home scent, no ant, not by the nest; stub = 1-2 adjacent open neighbours). Measured 0.6% of dug soil backfilled (harvester ants ~2.5%; Atta most). Without the 3 s wait carriers refilled their own just-dug cell (dig-fill churn, 53%, economy down). Next: pellets laying a building scent (Khuong 2016) to draw digging; a slower 'unused' test (scent fading over minutes) for Atta-like colonies; species parameter.
close_reason: MR12: leaf-cutter backfill. Unused judged against the path (scent < 0.5x the carrier's cell, never above it), fillable = any open cell whose open neighbours form one run (chamber edges, wide-tunnel sides, dead ends; never cuts a passage), carriers turn into stale branches and fill them from the tip, fresh pellets draw more (building scent, tau 60 s). Seeds 1-5, 600 s: 53.3% of dug soil refilled (MR11 0.6%), food home ~990/colony (-12%), ants out >120 s 0.7-1.7% (1.5-13.6%). PRD 17 part 3.

title: Co-infection: strains compete inside a host (today the first strain holds it)
description: fungus.ts: a host keeps the strain that infected it first; another strain's contact or brush dose adds load under the first strain's traits. Fine while there are two strains and one brush, but painting Lockpick into a Bloom-infected colony silently does nothing strain-wise. Options: per-strain load (a small array per ant), or strain replacement when the incoming strain's load share passes a threshold. Changes the per-ant state size; measure colony-bench worst case before and after.

title: A Start reply that lands after the page unmounts leaves the run open (picture and colony Jev clients)
description: Round 3 of the review of #2: click Colony while Start's POST /api/run is still waiting; at unmount the phase is idle so no stop is sent; when the reply lands start() sets running and starts timers on the disposed scheduler (2 /api/jev calls in 4 s, answers never saved). Fix: a #disposed flag that start() checks after its await (send a stop and return). Same pattern in ColonyJev.start.

title: Move the field's gesture logic into a pure, tested module
description: Review of #6. Click vs drag slop (use net displacement, not total path), pick reach, pinch hand-off, what ends a follow, fitted/zoomedIn flags, minimap hit test, brush scale: all inside ColonyField.tsx with no tests.

title: Keyboard access to following an ant and to the minimap
description: Review of #6. Arrows/WASD/+/-/0/n cover the camera; there is no keyboard way to pick an ant (e.g. cycle nearest ants with Tab/F) or to use the minimap.

title: The player's colony ticks first and wins every contested food pickup
description: Review of #4. game.ts ticks colonies in order. Alternate the order per tick, or resolve pickups after both have moved.

title: World generation may favour the player (nest central, rival at the edge of reach)
description: Review of #4: in a 10-seed sweep the player won 4, the rival led 2. Measure food within walking distance of each nest and balance placement.

title: Validate cached Jev answers loaded from localStorage (modes and stances); make the loader testable
description: Reviews of #3/#4. Any string is accepted as a Mode/Stance; a bad value becomes a permanent hit and STANCES.indexOf(-1) would corrupt encode. Filter per lane; move the loader out of the React hook so node --test covers it; consider pruning old custom-doctrine keys and two tabs overwriting each other.

title: avoid() treats rock or the map edge (-1) as the weakest alarm, steering ants into walls
description: Review of #3. Count rock/edge as +Infinity (or clamp to 0) when choosing the least-alarmed sensor.

title: Keep bd across cloud sessions: add it to the environment setup script
description: Containers are ephemeral. Add to the environment's setup script: apt-get install -y libicu-dev && (command -v bd || go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@v1.3.2). Owner: the user (environment settings).

title: MR 13: world events and fungus powers
description: Rain/flood/drought, antlion pits, bird, myrmecophile beetle; unlockable fungus brushes (propaganda, rain, decoy food, spore wall); flight/tournament spectacle; documentary follow-cam; time-lapse GIF export.

title: MR 11: castes and species wave 2
description: Per-ant caste; traits/*.ts hooks. Leafcutter (fungus garden, stridulation), weaver (territory marks), harvester (granary, return-rate), big-headed ant (enemy specification, absconding). Caste in the situation only for polymorphic species (×2).

title: MR 12: species wave 3, unusual life histories
description: Army ant (nomadic bivouac), Argentine ant (supercolony alliance), honeypot ant (repletes, tournaments), slave-maker (brood raids, propaganda). Tournament/raid strategist lane.

title: Fungus.configure alone changes the gate's menu without telling Jev
description: PR #7 review. React wiring calls both Fungus.configure and ColonyJev.setMenu; scripts or tests calling configure alone get Jev asked under a different menu than the gate runs. Make the menu one source (e.g. ColonyJev reads fungus.menu, or configure notifies).

title: ColonyJev: a colony without its own doctrine follows colony 0's only at the next game
description: PR #7 review. attachColonies gives colony k #doctrines[k] ?? #doctrines[0] without storing it; setDoctrineFor(0) later leaves colony k on the old words until the next attach. The UI always sets both; API callers and scripts hit it.

title: Spore counter counts cells too faint to see
description: The Fungus panel's "spores N cells" counts every cell above the 1e-3 the fungus forgets spores at, but the field draws spores only above ~0.06 (sp > 0.02 of 3). After a whole-map sweep it read "119,925 cells" with nothing violet on the ground. Count cells at or above the drawn threshold (a pass over #sporeCells), or show the total spores instead of a cell count.

title: Minimap: show spores and infected ants
description: ColonyField's minimap (paintMini) draws ground, food and both colonies' ants, but not the fungus: spore cells and infected ants only show in the main view. Tint infected ants in --spore on the minimap and wash spore cells, so the player sees spread across the whole map.

title: Small maps: some seeds place no food (under ~100×60)
description: Round 2 review of #5: at 100×60 seed 15 and 64×64 seed 12 have no food; at 40×30 the fallback rival nest can be 8 cells from the player's. The default 512×320 (and 1024×640) is clean. Scale patch density/min distance to small maps or guarantee at least one patch.

title: PRD §9 numbers don't reproduce with the UI's seeding
description: Review of #2: food home 32-92 % (PRD 49-86 %), seed 1 at 60 s 866 (PRD 1,077), situations seen 54-57 (PRD ~30), mode choices 3,300-4,200/s early (PRD 500-2,000). State the RNG used or update the numbers.

title: Seed input: clearing the field forces 1 and every keystroke regenerates the world
description: Review of #2. Commit the seed on blur/Enter; allow an empty field while typing.

title: Follow card: record who decided when the ant chose, not at render time
description: Review of #6. explain(q) runs at render; while paused, pressing Stop Jev relabels a Jev-decided ant as 'local rule'. Record the deciding source on the colony when the policy answers.

title: Small edge cases in the game outcome and enemy counts
description: Review of #4: both colonies beaten in the same tick shows 'lost' (a draw?); the enemy grid and enemiesNearNest count ants killed this tick for one tick.

title: Field goes soft when the window moves to a screen with a different DPR
description: ColonyField sizes its canvas from devicePixelRatio only on ResizeObserver; moving between monitors changes DPR without a CSS resize, so the picture is blurry until the next resize. Already so before MR 6. Fix: also listen to matchMedia('(resolution: Xdppx)') changes.
